research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2351, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1922, T-1923 refine in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2110-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2110-front, s35-2110-wing) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-066 (Rees Romanesque narrow house); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 25.500, v -2.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Romanesque' overlaid with the frontage row: The Harriet Rees house (Cobb & Frost, 1888) at its historical 2110 site, not its present one: the register's 'limestone front, tall gable' as a steep gable whose end faces the avenue over the 3B narrow body and its stone front, two bays wide. Its carved tympanum, loggia and bowed oriel are T-1922's and T-1923's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 4252346595 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
